paragraphs: Decision center: The work of a document management specialist is to turn front-end conditions such as the organization's files and records, the electronic content produced in business systems, and the constraints of law and classification level and retention periods into a management chain that can be executed, picked up by colleagues and users, and reviewed by audit and the competent authorities — first take part in determining document management policy and the classification scheme and check classification level and metadata and retrieval requirements, then configure system functions and permissions and version control according to the rules and implement capture and digitization, then deliver electronic assets to the users who need them through retrieval and distribution and handle access problems, then track regulations and retention periods and organize expiry appraisal and destruction, and finally record technical functions and specifications and performance data and hand off pending items and anomalies clearly. The focus of judgment is not whether you can scan all files into the system, but whether every step of the set-rules—configure-system—manage-permissions—capture—retrieve—control-retention-and-destruction—document chain is checkable, traceable and carried out within authorization and compliance requirements.

Good to try first: Able to relay requirements between business staff and technical colleagues while staying accurate; willing to work according to the rules and classification and metadata requirements and keep records; able to make judgments under compliance and classification and privacy constraints while restraining scope; able to work at a screen for long periods handling ledgers and configuration and records, and accept a rhythm driven by projects or system go-live milestones.

Proceed with caution: If you expect this job to be typing for others or general secretarial work, or are unwilling to work according to policy and the classification scheme and permission rules (granting permissions by impression, skipping metadata and version records, expanding retrieval and copying scope without authorization), or treat being familiar with a cloud drive or office software as professional document management ability, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: Using the fictional policy draft, classification scheme and document samples provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of classifying 12 documents by classification level and retention period and marking metadata, configuring access permissions for 3 user types, and writing a retrieval request handling and expiry appraisal and destruction ledger. This only verifies whether you are willing to check off rules and classification and permissions and retention item by item and document truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not touch real organizational files or personal information or classified content, makes no compliance or legal or security conclusions, and is not equivalent to position training or system authorization.

Decision center: Whether the organization's files and records and legal constraints can be organized into a document and records management chain that business staff and technical colleagues can pick up and review.

The workplace is offices and machine rooms or system operating environments, and the rhythm is determined by system go-live and migration and audit and record expiry milestones.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: This page is O*NET-SOC 15-1299.03 Document Management Specialists. Adjacent positions have different duties — computer and information systems managers are responsible for the overall information technology strategy and budget and team and system portfolio; administrative services managers are responsible for the coordinated management of institutional administrative affairs and facilities and procurement and records services; compliance managers are responsible for establishing the compliance system and regulatory communication and violation investigations; management consultants provide analytical methods and recommendations for organizational problems; computer systems analysts handle system requirements and design and implementation linkage; archivists are responsible for the collection and appraisal and arrangement and provision of archives; database administrators are responsible for database deployment and backup and performance and permission operations; information security analysts are responsible for security protection and incident response. The focus of this occupation is document and records management: setting policy and classification, configuring systems and permissions and versions, capturing and retrieving and distributing, controlling retention and destruction, and writing specifications and performance and documentation. Classified and compliance and privacy and security conclusions are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction and this organization's rules, are not inferred from the job title, and no one may issue legal or compliance or security opinions externally beyond their authorization.

Inputs that must be checked: document management policy and the classification scheme and metadata specifications, requirements for classification level and trade secrets and personal information and retention periods, electronic files produced by business and office systems and their formats and interfaces, user access and retrieval and copying needs and the scope of authorization, system versions and permissions and audit logs and backup arrangements, and expiry appraisal and destruction lists and approval records. What must not be done: do not grant permissions by impression or alter version records, do not skip metadata and retrieval and classification requirements, do not expand retrieval and copying and distribution scope without authorization or take classified or personal information content out of the approved environment, do not conceal or delay reporting archive damage and information leakage and security hazards, and do not use organizational files and user data for purposes other than work.

The fit judgment should be made by considering whether you can relay requirements between business and technology while staying accurate, whether you can work according to policy and classification and permission and retention, whether you can restrain scope under compliance and classification and privacy constraints, whether you can work at a screen for long periods handling ledgers and configuration and records, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization boundaries; it should not be replaced by a self-assessment of being able to use a document program or being familiar with file formats; all of these must be confirmed in supervised actual positions and a trial period.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real document and records management, permission configuration, and handling of classified and personal information and expiry appraisal and destruction must be carried out by personnel who have been trained and hold the corresponding authorization, in accordance with this organization's rules and the laws of the jurisdiction; the transfer and appraisal and destruction of archives and accounting archives have separate special procedures and supervised destruction requirements. Individuals may not issue legal, compliance, privacy or security conclusions externally beyond their authorization, and this page does not constitute legal, compliance, privacy, security or archive management advice.

The work object of this occupation is the organization's files and records and their management systems: policy and classification scheme and metadata specifications, electronic content produced by business and office systems and their formats and interfaces, classification level and retention period and destruction requirements, user and department access and retrieval and distribution needs, system functions and permissions and versions and audit logs and backups, and technical functions and specifications; some positions also involve performance data. The output is management results that make organizational files and records controllable, findable and compliant: executable document management policy and classification scheme, system functions and access permissions and version control configured according to the rules, retrievable and traceable electronic assets and their metadata, records of retention periods and expiry appraisal and destruction, and checkable technical specifications and handoff; some positions also produce system performance reports. The basis for judgment is document management policy and classification and metadata specifications, classification level and retention period and legal requirements, and this organization's rules and authorization rules — not personal habit or job title.

Judgment one: Are policy and classification clear and usable — do you take part in determining document management policy and the classification scheme and metadata specifications, and identify and classify documents by classification level and function and metadata, rather than classifying by impression?

Judgment two: Are systems and configuration implemented according to the rules — do you work with information technology staff to implement electronic document processing and retrieval and distribution systems, and configure user interfaces and access configuration files and document workflows as prescribed?

Judgment three: Are permissions and versions held — do you manage access permissions and version control, record changes to official documents and confirm them with legal and compliance and records management staff, rather than defaulting to visible to everyone or letting versions get confused?

Judgment four: Are capture and retrieval and distribution traceable — do you implement scanning and automatic data entry and digitization to specification, and can you retrieve electronic assets within the scope of authorization and distribute them to users with documentation?

Judgment five: Are regulations and retention periods and destruction keeping up — do you track developments in records and document management regulations, organize expiry appraisal and destruction according to retention periods, and keep appraisal opinions and destruction records?

Judgment six: Are authorization and security and handoff held — do you handle access and retrieval and distribution and exceptions within the scope of authorization, report archive damage and information leakage and security hazards promptly, and write support documents and training materials and hand off pending items and anomalies clearly?

The work of document management specialists can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is policy and classification and requirements: take part in determining document management policy, establish document and content classification schemes to support information capture and retrieval, identify and classify documents by classification level and function and metadata, conduct needs assessments to identify the document management requirements of departments and end users, and write standards and best practices and system usage procedures. The second is systems and configuration and capture: work with other information technology professionals to implement electronic document processing and retrieval and distribution systems, assist in evaluating and procuring and deploying new systems, configure user interfaces and access configuration files and document workflows, implement access permissions and version control, operate data capture technologies (including scanning and imaging and automatic data entry) to import digitized documents into the system, and exercise security oversight over document processing and copying and distribution and storage and archiving. The third is retrieval and compliance and support: retrieve electronic assets from the repository within the scope of authorization and distribute them to users, advise end users on electronic content access issues and provide support documents and training materials, monitor regulatory developments and retention periods and organize appraisal and destruction on schedule, write system test plans and technical functions and specifications, and in some positions analyze and interpret system performance data (a supplemental task). All three work areas proceed within policy and the classification scheme, classification level and retention periods, and this organization's rules and authorization rules.

When doing this job, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be checked?

Common errors cluster into four categories: first, policy and classification are not clearly set before starting, making metadata and retrieval scopes inconsistent; second, system and permission and version configuration do not follow the rules, causing unauthorized access or confused versions; third, capture and retrieval and distribution are not documented, making sources and destinations untraceable; fourth, retention periods and appraisal and destruction do not keep up, so what should be kept is not kept or what should be destroyed is not destroyed. The checking method is that each item has a reviewable basis: the version of policy and classification and metadata specifications, records of system functions and permissions and version control and audit logs, digitization and data capture and retrieval and distribution records, and retention period and appraisal and destruction inventories and approval records — not memory or verbal understanding.

facts.display_value: Note: the Chinese mainland has no unified occupational qualification corresponding one-to-one with United States 15-1299.03, and requirements are distinguished by rules and regulations. Document and electronic archive management is governed by the Archives Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted on revision June 20, 2020, effective January 1, 2021): Party and government organs, groups, enterprises and institutions and other organizations should actively advance the construction of electronic archive management information systems, interconnected with office automation systems and business systems; electronic archives should have reliable provenance and standardized procedures and compliant elements, and electronic archives have the same effect as archives on traditional carriers and may be used as evidence in electronic form; the state encourages and supports advancing the digitization of archives on traditional carriers, and those already digitized should have their originals properly preserved; electronic archives should be transferred to archives institutions through networks or storage media that meet security management requirements, and archives institutions should test the electronic archives they receive to ensure their authenticity and integrity and usability and security, and may store important electronic archives in backup at a different location; the competent archives department may inspect archive informatization construction and information security assurance, must promptly remediate archive security hazards found, and must report promptly in cases such as archive damage and information leakage. Accounting archives are governed by the Measures for the Administration of Accounting Archives (Ministry of Finance and National Archives Administration Decree No. 79, effective January 1, 2016): retention periods are divided into permanent and periodic, and periodic retention periods are generally divided into 10 years and 30 years and run from the first day after the end of the accounting year; on expiry an appraisal should be conducted and an accounting archive appraisal opinion formed, destruction should follow procedures to prepare a destruction inventory and be signed and jointly supervised by dispatched personnel, and accounting vouchers for claims and debts not yet settled at the end of the retention period may not be destroyed. Classified documents and network and data and personal information security follow the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets and the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China and the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (parts other than the above specific regulations are cited by name and general requirements, and article numbers were not checked item by item). Positions related to this occupation are spread across different industries such as information and technical services, finance and insurance, health care and education, public administration and manufacturing, and pay is determined by the unit's and position's rules; public wage statistics are broken down at most to industry category and unit type, and no occupation-level scope corresponding to this occupation has been established, so no verifiable Chinese mainland occupation-level wage distribution was obtained in this round

description.text: Document Management Specialists (O*NET-SOC 15-1299.03) do file and records management in organizations that rely on large volumes of electronic records, such as information and technical services, finance and insurance, health care and education, public administration and manufacturing: take part in determining document management policy and the classification scheme and metadata specifications, jointly implement and configure the functions and access permissions and version control and document workflows of document and content management systems, operate scanning and imaging and automatic data entry to implement capture and digitization, retrieve and distribute electronic assets within the scope of authorization and provide support and training materials, monitor regulatory developments and retention periods and organize expiry appraisal and destruction, and write system test plans and technical functions and specifications and analyze system performance data. United States scope: the wages and employment for this detailed occupation are taken from the parent group Computer Occupations, All Other (15-1299) proxy scope — the 2025 wage data parent group median is 116,580 US dollars per year (56.05 US dollars per hour), with annual percentiles of 55,940／79,370／116,580／157,500／188,470 US dollars; employment was about 472,000 in 2024, the 2024—2034 projection is much faster than average (7% or higher), with about 31,300 projected openings; the detailed occupation preparation level is Job Zone Four and the interest code is CI. Chinese mainland: files and electronic archives are managed under the Archives Law of the People's Republic of China, accounting archives under the Measures for the Administration of Accounting Archives, and classified and data and personal information under the relevant regulations; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.name: Document management specialists
subject.summary: Document Management Specialists (United States side, O*NET-SOC 15-1299.03) is an organizational file and records management position: implementing and administering enterprise-wide document management systems and related procedures so that organizations can capture, store, retrieve, share and destroy electronic records and documents; taking part in determining document management policy and establishing document and content classification schemes, identifying and classifying documents by classification level and function and metadata and developing standards and best practices and system usage procedures, conducting needs assessments and working with other information technology professionals to implement electronic document processing and retrieval and distribution systems; managing access permissions and version control, recording changes to official documents and confirming them with legal and compliance and records management staff, configuring user interfaces and access configuration files and document workflows, operating scanning and imaging and automatic data entry to implement capture and digitization and exercising security oversight over document processing and copying and distribution and storage and archiving; retrieving electronic assets within the scope of authorization and distributing them to users and providing support documents and training materials, monitoring regulatory developments and retention periods and organizing expiry appraisal and destruction, and writing system test plans and technical functions and specifications and analyzing system performance data. United States scope: the wages and employment and projections for this detailed occupation are taken from the parent group Computer Occupations, All Other (15-1299) proxy scope — the BLS 2025 wage data parent group median is 116,580 US dollars per year (56.05 US dollars per hour), with annual percentiles of 55,940／79,370／116,580／157,500／188,470 US dollars (hourly percentiles 26.89／38.16／56.05／75.72／90.61); the O*NET summary page gives employment of about 472,000 in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of much faster than average (7% or higher) and about 31,300 projected job openings (the source gives only the category and threshold and not a single precise percentage, and this page states it in the original wording); the detailed occupation scope is: preparation level Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), interest code CI, education feedback of 60% bachelor's degree and 15% master's degree and 10% associate's or two-year degree, and 23 tasks; the work context includes use email every day 100%, telephone conversations every day 74%, face-to-face discussions every day 59%, continuous contact with others 16% (another 47% in contact most of the time), teamwork extremely important 33%, decision freedom very much 20%, precision or accuracy extremely important 35%, facing time pressure every day 20%, making decisions every day 16%, working hours regular (fixed schedule) 95%, continuous sitting 35% (another 50% more than half the time), and dealing with external customers or the public very important 26%. Chinese mainland scope: file and electronic archive management follows the Archives Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2020, effective January 1, 2021), and electronic archives should have reliable provenance and standardized procedures and compliant elements and have the same effect as archives on traditional carriers; accounting archives follow the Measures for the Administration of Accounting Archives (Ministry of Finance and National Archives Administration Decree No. 79, effective January 1, 2016); classified documents and network and data and personal information security follow the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets and the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China and the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (parts other than the above specific regulations are cited by name and general requirements, and article numbers were not checked item by item); this occupation has no uniform access-type professional qualification in the Chinese mainland. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope corresponding to this occupation, and this page truthfully retains the gap.
